seo.metaTitle: Wrongful Death Lawyer in Portola Valley, CA
seo.metaDescription: Lost a loved one in Portola Valley? Our team helps families pursue wrongful death claims under California law. Free consultation. A 2-year deadline applies.

hero.subtitle: When a death in Portola Valley was caused by someone else's carelessness, your family may have a civil claim under California law. We can help you understand your rights and pursue recovery.

about.title: Portola Valley Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Portola Valley is a small town — fewer than 5,000 residents along the wooded stretch of San Mateo County where Alpine Road, Portola Road, Westridge Drive and Arastradero Road carry most of the local traffic. Public records for 2025 show 11 injury collisions and 13 people hurt here, with no traffic deaths that year. Numbers like those are a comfort until they are not; a fatal crash, a fall on someone else's property, or a medical error can reach a family just as it can anywhere. When it does, California law gives certain survivors the right to bring a civil wrongful death claim. That claim runs on its own track, separate from any criminal case, and it must generally be filed within two years of the death — sooner if a public agency is involved. We handle wrongful death cases in San Mateo County and work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Portola Valley Choose Us

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can sort out who in your family has the right to bring the claim before anything is filed.

items.title: Help meeting a firm deadline
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or other government entity may be responsible. Getting in touch early protects your options.

items.title: Losses measured honestly
items.desc: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. We work on contingency, so you owe nothing unless there is a recovery.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash on Alpine Road is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that is separate from any criminal prosecution, and it can move forward on its own timeline. Waiting for the criminal case to finish can eat into the two-year filing window, so it is worth speaking with us sooner rather than later. We can also explain how evidence from the criminal matter may be used in your civil claim.

items.question: My sibling died and had no spouse or children. Can I bring a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. California gives first priority to a spouse or domestic partner and children, but when there are none, certain other heirs and financially dependent family members may have standing. Whether you qualify depends on your relationship and the specifics of your situation, which we can review with you at no charge.

items.question: Portola Valley recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Are wrongful death claims here only about car crashes?
items.answer: Not at all. Wrongful death claims arise from many situations — a fall on poorly maintained property, a medical error, a defective product, or neglect in a care facility, among others. If you believe another person or business caused your loved one's death anywhere in San Mateo County, we can help you evaluate it.
